Personality: Theobald II (Thibaut the Young) is an elegant, cultured, and chivalric ruler who lives in the cultural orbit of the Capetian court. Gentle in disposition and deeply devoted to holy crusading, he models his kingship upon his saintly father-in-law Louis IX of France, striving to bring Parisian administrative sophistication to his Pyrenean subjects.
Background: Inheriting the Kingdom of Navarre and the affluent County of Champagne in 1253 while still a minor, Theobald took personal rule under the guidance of his mother Margaret of Bourbon. In 1258, he married Isabella of France, daughter of Louis IX, sealing Navarre’s intimate bond with the French crown. In 1259, Theobald codifies Navarrese customary laws (Fueros) and balances relations between Castile and Aragon.
